newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 23.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wendesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NATION
- Pakistan Law Commission has observed that there was no need for creating special courts for quick dispensation of justice.
- Japan has asked Pakistan to take a lead and sign Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty (CTBT) even before India does.
- Execution of two Christian convicts for murder was stopped by President Farooq Leghari.
- Police in the central province of Punjab arrested 170 people from a school run by Shi'ite Moslem group in Lahore.
- A joint session of the parliament will be convened on August 14 to mark the 50th anniversary of Pakistan.
- The Supreme Court received a petition from a citizen calling upon the court to take notice of the death of two cadets allegedly due to ragging while training at an air force school.
DAWN

- Many previous records were broken on the Karachi Stock Exchange on Tuesday as the index soared 104.06 points, or 5.44 percent, and closed at 2,016.51 and market capitalisation hit an all-time peak at 609 billion rupees.

- The visiting International Monetary Fund senior director, Paul Chabrier, held wide-ranging talks with deputy chairman planning commission Hafeez Pasha with a view to conclude talks on the new $1.5 billion enhanced structural adjustment facilty.
- Some top level changes in the Sindh administration are expected following the arrival of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif in Karachi.

- The government is evolving a strategy to substitute gas for oil in power generation, reduce import of oil, avoid counter productive investment in oil import infrastructure, import natural gas and increase production of indigenous gas.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan is contemplating lowering its discount and repo rates to bring it closer to the market rates.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government has selected Beicip Franlab of France for awarding the contrct of Advisory Technical Assistance study on import of gas.
- The United States has agreed to provide Pakistan with wheat worth $20 million in addition to soybean meal of $10 million under the PL-480 package.
FINANCIAL POST

- Japanese investors are willing to enter into joint ventures with Pakistani businessmen, provided they are assured of protection of their investment and consistency in government's policies, says a spokesman for the Japanese Foreign Ministry.
-- Islamabad Newsroom 274757
